critical_code_review_comments: Restoring theme.palette.secondary to a neutral SURFACE token (light #F4F6FA / dark #1E1E28) was the right root-cause fix — it decouples the lime ACCENT (primary/success) from the many card BACKGROUNDS that were incorrectly picking it up. All the follow-on invisible items (sidebar ReferralCard, referrals step chips, PanelCard header pills, RadioGroup, CustomSwitch, wallet chips) resolved from this single palette correction, which is cleaner than patching each component's fg/bg pair.
Consider adding a Storybook / Chromatic contrast lint check on both themes in CI to prevent regressions the next time the accent palette is retuned.
Landing homeTheme text.disabled at #71717A on light bg still barely misses AA for small text; #5B5B66 or #6B6B78 would give ~5:1.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fixes verified end-to-end. Approach: (1) contrast auditor compares element color against nearest ancestor with opaque bg (alpha>=0.9) to avoid alpha-composite false positives that plagued iteration_22. (2) Theme toggle via localStorage.setItem('theme-mode',...)+reload (button click flaky). (3) Wait ~10s after route change for Next dev compile. Only remaining nit is landing light captions at 4.27:1 (marginal).
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: secondary.main had been overloaded with the lime accent, which then bled into all surfaces that used it as a background (sidebar ReferralCard, referrals step chips, various PanelCards) while their child text tokens (either near-black in light or white/gray in dark) remained unchanged, producing 1:1 or near-1:1 contrast. Fix: restored secondary palette to a neutral SURFACE token (light #F4F6FA, dark #1E1E28); primary/success remain the true lime/near-black accents used sparingly with explicit contrastText. This is now verified across /dashboard, /wallet, /transactions, /developer-keys, /referrals, sidebar promo card, landing home theme, and the celebration modal (correctly suppressed for existing merchant).
